points.description: Selects/finds the k nearest existing data points that already have a class/colour (e.g. by constructing a sphere around the new point containing k neighbours). Equivalent wording such as 'look at the k closest labelled examples' earns the mark.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if nearest neighbours are mentioned but k or the use of already-classified old data is missing/unclear.

levels.says: Mentions nearest neighbours or old/classified data, but does not make clear that the k nearest already-classified points are selected.

points.description: Takes a majority vote / maximum count among the classes (colours) of those k neighbours and assigns the new data point to the class with the most votes. Equivalent wording such as 'choose the most common label among the neighbours' earns the mark.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if voting/majority class is mentioned but the new point is not clearly assigned to the winning class.

levels.says: Mentions voting or the majority class among neighbours, but does not clearly state that the new point is assigned to that winning class.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both central steps: find the k nearest already-classified neighbours and assign the new point to the class with the most votes among them. A clear pseudocode listing or a prose description of the same steps earns the marks; pseudocode syntax is not marked. The reference's phrase 'unsupervised manner' is not required, and marks depend on the neighbour-selection and majority-vote procedure.
